rationale: The base station auto-updated to firmware 4.5, which dropped protocol v2 support, while the guest room CAM-I2 (hardware revision A, firmware 1.2) still speaks v2. check_firmware_compat confirms no OTA path to v3 exists for this hardware revision, and logs show "E-305 protocol v2 not supported" plus "OTA unavailable for hardware revision A". This matches historical case H-03, which required FAE escalation for a compatibility firmware.

output.symptom_summary: Guest room camera (CAM-I2) went offline overnight and remains offline with orange LED. App shows no update available. Base station online with error E-305.
output.suspected_root_cause: Protocol conflict: base station auto-updated to firmware 4.5 dropping protocol v2 support, while CAM-I2 hardware revision A firmware 1.2 only supports v2 and has no OTA path to v3.

results.text: The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

results.source: historical_cases#H-03 Indoor camera lost after night update
results.text: After HB-200 auto-updated to 4.5, a CAM-I2 running 1.2 disconnected with E-305. OTA not offered for this hardware revision. Escalated; FAE confirmed protocol v2 dropped and arranged a compatibility firmware. Escalated correctly.

Peripheral firmware is upgraded over the air (OTA) from the base station. Requirements: device within normal signal range, battery above 30 percent. CAM-S1 1.x upgrades to 2.1 (protocol v3). SEN-D1 1.0 upgrades to 1.3, SEN-M1 1.1 upgrades to 1.4. CAM-I2 hardware revision A with firmware 1.2 cannot be upgraded to protocol v3.

complaint: The guest room camera went offline overnight and won't come back. It is a wired indoor camera and has power; the LED is orange. A friend who works in IT told me to factory reset the base station, but I'd rather not lose all my settings. I looked in the app for a camera update and it says none is available.
usability_reason: The response is polite and clearly summarizes symptoms, but it is not actionable: it tells the customer no action is needed and defers to engineering without any concrete next step. It also presents detailed diagnostic claims (firmware versions, protocol conflict, error E-305, RSSI) that are not supported by the session record, which shows no questions asked and no actions performed. The root-cause label is asserted without evidence of completed checks.
